candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: use aseptic technique, maintain invasive devices safely, and implement measures to prevent healthcare-associated infection.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — CAUTI prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Prevent CAUTI by limiting indwelling catheter use to valid indications, maintaining a continuously closed and unobstructed drainage system, and reassessing daily for prompt removal rather than using routine antimicrobial prophylaxis or unnecessary system disconnections.

options.A: Verify that a valid indication remains, maintain an intact closed drainage system with unobstructed flow, and remove the catheter as soon as it is no longer needed.
options.B: Disconnect the drainage tubing daily for routine cleaning and reconnect it after the tubing has air-dried.
options.C: Continue the catheter for staff convenience when the client is incontinent even if no other clinical indication remains.
options.D: Use routine systemic antibiotics and antiseptic meatal cleaning while the catheter remains in place to prevent bacteriuria.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. CDC recommends inserting urinary catheters only for appropriate indications, leaving them in place only as long as needed, maintaining a closed drainage system after aseptic insertion, keeping urine flow unobstructed, and using quality-improvement processes such as daily review to identify catheters that can be removed. B breaks the closed system without a clinical indication. C is specifically listed as inappropriate catheter use when the catheter substitutes for incontinence care. D is incorrect because CDC does not recommend routine systemic antimicrobials for CAUTI prevention and recommends routine hygiene rather than antiseptic periurethral cleaning while the catheter is in place.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CAUTI prevention requires appropriate catheter indication, aseptic insertion, maintenance of a closed unobstructed drainage system, and prompt removal when no longer needed; routine antimicrobial prophylaxis and antiseptic meatal cleaning are not recommended.
candidate.source_document_title: Clinical Safety: Preventing Catheter-associated Urinary Tract Infections (CAUTIs); Guideline for Prevention of Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infections — Summary of Recommendations
candidate.source_locator: Clinical Safety recommendations: use urinary catheters only when needed, place using aseptic technique/sterile equipment, maintain the closed sterile drainage system, and remove as soon as no longer needed. Summary of Recommendations I.A: insert only for appropriate indications and leave only as long as needed; III.A and III.B: maintain a closed drainage system and unobstructed urine flow; III.F and III.G: do not routinely use systemic antimicrobials or antiseptic periurethral cleaning for CAUTI prevention; IV.A: use QI strategies including daily review of continued need and removal of unnecessary catheters.
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.source_version_date: Clinical Safety page dated June 27, 2025; CAUTI guideline web pages current through 2024; accessed 2026-08-17
